AIP Congress 2026 — Program Explorer 7–11 Dec 2026

26th Australian Institute of Physics Congress, co-locating with the Australian & New Zealand Conference on Optics and Photonics (ANZCOP), with COMMAD as a dedicated topical track.

📅 Monday 7 – Friday 11 December 2026 (registration from Sunday 6 Dec) 📍 Belinda Hutchinson Building, The University of Sydney 🕑 All times AEDT (Australia/Sydney) 🔍 Press / to search
Official program page Register Activities & social events Speakers Workshops Source timetable (Indico)
Congress highlights
Public lecture
Dr Jessie Christiansen (NASA/Caltech)

Mon 7 Dec, evening. The hunt for Earth 2.0 — from the first exoplanets to NASA's next flagship telescope. Free, open to all.

Public lecture
Dr Derek Muller (Veritasium)

Thu 10 Dec, evening. From Physics PhD to YouTuber: what Veritasium learned about explaining the universe.

Social highlight
Congress Dinner on the Harbour

Wed 9 Dec. Three-hour Sydney Harbour cruise with the AIP & ANZOS award ceremonies. Tickets via registration.

Friday programs
Teachers Day & Career Fair

Fri 11 Dec. Australian Physics Teachers Day (from 8am) and the Australian Physics Career Fair (1–4pm).

About this page

An independent, mobile-friendly view of the AIP Congress 2026 program, built from the official Indico timetable (event 16926), retrieved 19 November 2026. Session and talk titles are as published; a few obvious typos were corrected.

Times, rooms and abstracts can still change — always confirm on the official pages close to the event.

Tips

Pick a day tab to focus, or All week for the full program. Search matches every word in any order, ignoring accents (e.g. dzurak silicon) — put “quotes” around words for an exact phrase; matches are highlighted. If a day has no matches, results from the rest of the week appear automatically. Click a group badge (e.g. QST, NUPP) to filter to that group. Star individual talks or whole sessions, then open My agenda to see them in a list or calendar, export them, or share them as a link. Short forms of institutions work too (unsw, anu, usyd). Participants lists every speaker and convener by institution. During the congress, Now jumps to what is on.

The page address keeps your day, search and filters, so you can bookmark or share a view. Once loaded, the page also works offline.
